character: Dr. Ptahsheptut Smith's private alibi interview
voice: Educated, imposing, guarded, and affronted without pulp exoticism; Laura is direct and increasingly skeptical.

entries.text: Good evening, Dr. Smith.
Miss Bow. I did not expect to see you here.
But I expected you.
You did? How?
That isn't important. Why are you here?
I had an appointment with Dr. Carter.
You know that he is dead.
Dead? I had not heard.
He died in this room. I'm surprised the news escaped you.
I am shocked. I do not know what to say.
Then tell me where you were at eight o'clock, when he died.
At the party, of course. You saw me there.
Not at eight o'clock.
Then I must have been answering that telephone call.
What telephone call?
Mr. Heimlich said a call was waiting on Dr. Carrington's telephone. When I reached the office, the line was dead, so I returned to the party.
Was Dr. Carrington in his office?
No. He was at the party.
Did Mr. Heimlich say who was calling?
No. He did not take the call, and I do not know who informed him of it.
You and Dr. Carter argued frequently about the Dagger of Amon Ra.
We disagreed, yes.
Did you kill him?
Miss Bow, I am appalled that you would ask me such a thing. This interview is over.
We'll speak again later.
